newsitem.title: FRANCE: Japan nuclear waste ship to take southern route.
newsitem.headline: Japan nuclear waste ship to take southern route.

text.p: A ship carrying processed nuclear waste from France to Japan will skirt Africa and sail through the southwest Pacific to reach the port of Mutsu Ogawara by mid-March, the reprocessing company said on Tuesday.
The French state company COGEMA disclosed the shipment's route a day after the British freighter Pacific Teal left the French Channel port of Cherbourg.
It gave no other details than saying the ship would sail around the Cape of Good Hope at the southern tip of Africa, across the Indian Ocean and through the southwest Pacific.
Two other routes, round Cape Horn to skirt South America, and through the Caribbean and the Panama Canal, were discarded.
New Zealand and other South Pacific nations have expressed concern that the ship's route will take it through their self-declared nuclear-free area.

The environmental group Greenpeace said a French diplomatic cable leaked in December indicated the ship would travel around the Cape of Good Hope, through the Tasman Sea between New Zealand and Australia and then north through the Pacific Ocean.
The waste initially came from Japan and was processed at La Hague under a deal between the French state company COGEMA (Compagnie Generale des Matieres Nucleaires) and 10 Japanese power companies.

It was the second such shipment to Japan from France. Environmental pressure group Greenpeace, which is protesting at the secrecy surrounding such shipments, said it expected 3,000 cargoes of plutonium waste to be moved over the next 10 to 15 years.
